reference.source: Dhingra Diseases of ENT 8th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Bacterial sinusitis: 10 days, severe start, or double worsening
Orbital warning: proptosis, ophthalmoplegia, vision change
Pott puffy tumour is frontal bone osteomyelitis
reference.pathophysiology: Mucociliary failure and ostial blockage stagnate secretions for bacterial growth, while valveless veins and paper thin lamina conduct infection to orbit and cavernous sinus, and diploic veins seed frontal bone and epidural spaces.
additionalDifferentials: Viral versus bacterial rhinosinusitis by duration pattern
Preseptal versus orbital cellulitis by eye movement and vision
additionalInvestigations: Nasendoscopy for meatal pus and polyps
Contrast CT orbits and sinuses for complications
MRI brain and sinuses for intracranial extension
